title.narrative: Advancing right-based accountable and responsible humanitarian practices through multi-sectorial assistance towards Southeastern conflict affected population

description.narrative: ltpgtThis 12-month project is based on a human-rights based approach, by prioritizing fundamental human rights of access to accountable and responsible services by conflict affected population. It will be a multi-sectorial one by offering protection, shelter/NFIs and food services to crisis affected civilians living in East Bago two townships (Kyauk Kyi and Shwe Gyin). Due to active conflict in those areas, there are significant humanitarian obstacles when it comes to service delivery, hindering access to services. In contrast, because of the military attacks in various ways: air strikes, indiscriminate killing, violation of human rights with abuses, multi-sectorial humanitarian needs are on rise. ltbrgtThe risks of protection including Child Protection (CP), Gender-Based Violence (GBV), Mine Risks and general protection have skyrocketed in the aftermath of the coup. Safety and security concerns, uncertainty and limited access to justice and legal aid have an impact on physical and emotional well-being of local conflict affected communities. To address this, the project has proposed individual protection service provision through cash and other necessary assistance and community-level group awareness raising sessions. ltbrgtIn light of political instability causing multiple and repeated displacement for local communities, even daily needs are unmet. Noticeably, getting Shelter/NFIs and food assistance are of paramount importance – which the project aims to support through cash-based programming. ltbrgtLocalization has been prioritized noticeably by promoting equitable partnership, adequate resourcing, motivating partner’s leadership and intending to build local capacity. As the chosen partner is from the grass-roots level: Committee for Internally Displaced Karen People (CIDKP) is a local ethnic Kayin organization, the partner has access to target areas, with well-established networks and experiences. ltbrgtAccountability to affected population will ensure through proper and functioning complaint and feedback mechanism, with communities’ meaningful participation starting from initial needs assessment to closure phase. Inclusion mainstreaming will be promoted across disability inclusion and protection mainstreaming of Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE). At the end, this multi-sectorial project aims to reach out to 9,615 communities (4,403 Men, 5,172 Women, 18 Boys and 22 Girls) including 1,250 persons with disabilities among total target (572 Men, 673 Women, 2 Boys, 3 Girls) living in 2 townships of East Bago region. ltbrgtlt/pgt
